en: The Sūtra on the Parable of the Consecrated King, spoken by the Buddha.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao Feng Da Fu, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices,
Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, and Recipient of the Purple Robe.
Translated by the subject Shi Hu and others, by imperial decree. At that time, the World-Honored One was in the kingdom of Śrāvastī; for a certain reason, he addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"You should know that there are three kṣatriya kings who, at three specific times, receive the royal consecration in a certain region.
These three kings constantly keep [this] in mind for as long as they live."
What are these three? They are as follows:
First, there is a king in the prime of his youth who, according to the rite of consecration, receives the royal empowerment in a certain region;
having received the empowerment, he constantly reflects upon it for as long as he lives.
Furthermore, the second king, whose power and merit gradually increased, received the royal consecration in a certain region according to the *abhiṣeka* rite;
having obtained this consecration, he constantly kept it in mind for as long as he lived.
Furthermore, the third king possesses great power and preeminence in martial valor; all his adversaries submit to him in faith.
Because he is most excellent, he dwells in victory and, according to the rite of consecration (*abhiṣeka*), receives the royal empowerment in a certain region.
Having received this empowerment, he constantly reflects upon it for as long as he lives.

“O bhikṣus, you too are just like this: at the three times of day, in a certain direction, you should perform the work of cultivation and realization, constantly keeping it in mind until the end of your lives.”
What are these three? They are:
there is a bhikṣu who, having conceived right faith, leaves the home life for homelessness, shaves off his hair and beard, and dons the saffron robes;
this is the first, regarding whom one dwells in a certain direction, practicing the duties of a bhikṣu, and constantly keeps him in mind throughout the rest of his life.
Furthermore, there was a bhikṣu who cultivated various sublime practices in order to realize cessation and thereby severed all phenomena of origination;
having known this, he became free from dust and removed from defilement, attaining the pure Dharma-eye regarding all phenomena.
This was the second [bhikṣu] who, residing in a certain region, performed the duties of a bhikṣu and constantly maintained such mindfulness until the end of his life.

Furthermore, there is a bhikṣu whose outflows are exhausted, in whom the outflows no longer increase, whose mind is well-liberated and whose wisdom is well-liberated; having realized this through his own knowledge and attained its fulfillment, he knows: "Birth has been exhausted, the holy life has been established, what was to be done has been accomplished, and there is no further existence.
This is the third matter concerning the realization of the noble fruit in a certain direction, which one should constantly keep in mind for as long as life lasts.
The Sūtra on the Parable of the Consecrated King, Spoken by the Buddha.
